items.title: Housing decree survives, but indefinite rentals fail
items.body: Congress's standing committee upheld the main housing decree on November 12, keeping tenant protections and tax changes in force. Until December 31, 2027, rents above the reference indices cannot rise; others can rise 2% at most without agreement. A second decree, on indefinite rentals, did not win enough support.

items.title: Retirement requirements tighten from January 1, 2027
items.body: Under the existing pension reform, retiring at 65 will require 38 years and six months of Social Security contributions from January 1, 2027. Anyone below that threshold must wait until 67. This final scheduled step responds to longer life expectancy and an ageing population.

items.title: Interior orders police to stop protest tear gas
items.body: Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska ordered police to stop using tear gas at demonstrations after unions complained about police action during the November 11 general strike. He also opened investigations separate from police internal checks. Provisional figures list 47 arrests, excluding Catalonia and the Basque Country.

items.title: Immigration brings Spain close to 50 million residents
items.body: Spain's population reached a record 49.94 million on October 1, 2026, and could pass 50 million in November or December. Immigration drives the growth, while the Spanish-born population shrinks as it ages. The foreign-born population rose by 520,000 in a year, to a record 10.43 million.

items.title: PP election platform proposes ending rent controls
items.body: For the November 29 election, the PP proposes repealing the Ley de Vivienda (housing law), including the decree upheld on November 12. It would replace rent controls with tax incentives, saying the current tools reduced the supply of homes. Repeal would require legislation; current rules remain in force.

items.title: Tax tribunal clarifies voluntary exit payout rules
items.body: A binding October 27 tax tribunal ruling treats voluntary exit payouts outside collective redundancy procedures as IRPF (personal income tax) income. It creates no new tax. Qualifying collective dismissals can keep exemptions up to 180,000 euros; some taxable payouts may qualify for a 30% reduction.

items.title: Rosalía wins five awards at Latin Grammys
items.body: Singer Rosalía won five Latin Grammys: album of the year for "Lux", song of the year and best pop song for "La Perla", best short video for "Sauvignon Blanc", and best alternative music album. It was her third album-of-the-year win, after 2019 and 2022.

items.title: Ministry demands removal of 8,352 tourist rental ads
items.body: The Consumer Affairs Ministry announced on November 12 that it demanded two large rental platforms remove 8,352 tourist-flat listings. Of these, 7,227 lack required identification, while 1,125 advertise whole homes using expired room-rental registration numbers.

items.title: France leans towards Spanish candidate for ECB
items.body: France is leaning towards backing former Bank of Spain governor Pablo Hernández de Cos as the next European Central Bank president, in exchange for a good seat on the board. Germany is less clear and nothing is settled. The key EU meeting is November 26-27. The ECB sets eurozone interest rates.

items.title: Plus Ultra announces redundancy plan covering 679 workers
items.body: Airline Plus Ultra has given notice of a collective redundancy process covering its 679 employees, citing worsening finances and operations. Formal consultations have yet to start, and the final number of job cuts is not set. The plan includes fewer aircraft and fewer routes between Spain and Latin America.

items.title: Blackout recovery costs scheduled for 2027 electricity bills
items.body: Under a regulator-approved payment method, Red Eléctrica has scheduled 29.15 million euros in blackout-recovery payments across 2027. The estimated cost for consumers is 0.12 euros per MWh. The old formula did not cover plants' costs; retailers say they lack legal backing to pass the charge on in most standard contracts.
